item.title: AI-Driven Intrusions, Danfoss Controller Flaws, and Critical Infrastructure Cyber Incidents
item.content:encoded:
Window: 16 Nov 11:00 → 16 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Six Unpatched Danfoss Refrigeration Controller Flaws Could Allow Remote Takeover Without Login — Should Read

Six unpatched flaws in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers could allow unauthenticated remote root-level takeover, including potentially bypassing Strict mode. Operators should immediately remove management interfaces from the public internet and use protected remote access, as no fix is currently available.

  • Researchers at Midnight Blue identified six flaws in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers that could allow a remote attacker to take control without logging in.
  • No patch has been published, and Midnight Blue said that the latest available AK-SM800A firmware, version 5.4.0, does not fix the reported flaws.
  • Five flaws are in unauthenticated web request handlers running as root, while a sixth affects the gateway that enforces the controller's Strict mode login protection.
  • Belgian, Irish, and German cybersecurity agencies advised operators to remove controller management interfaces from the public internet and use protected remote access instead.
  • An attacker with root-level control could alter refrigeration settings, trigger defrost cycles, conceal activity in logs, or install code that persists through a factory reset and firmware update.

Technologies: ics-scada, iot-device, remote-access

Products: ak-sm800a, strict-mode

Vendors: danfoss

Retadup Worm Resurfaces 7 Years After Takedown to Spread CoffeeLoader Malware — Should Read

The Retadup USB-spreading worm has resurfaced years after its 2019 takedown, with re-registered command-and-control domains now delivering the CoffeeLoader malware loader. CoffeeLoader uses GPU-assisted packing, persistence mechanisms, and process injection to fetch and execute further payloads.

  • Kaspersky identified a new CoffeeLoader variant delivered through the Retadup Windows worm, whose former command-and-control domains were re-registered and used to distribute third-party malware.
  • The new CoffeeLoader delivery chain uses a modified 7-Zip library containing self-decrypting code from an updated Armoury packer that uses OpenGL rather than OpenCL.
  • The CoffeeLoader downloader establishes automatic startup through Windows registry settings, copies itself into ProgramData or LocalAppData subfolders, and injects itself into legitimate Windows processes.
  • After connecting to a built-in control server, CoffeeLoader can run additional software by placing it inside another process, saving and launching an executable, or saving a library and launching it with rundll32.exe.
  • Kaspersky said it blocked roughly 15,000 systems from the revived Retadup infections, with most affected systems in Peru, Angola, Russia, and Bolivia.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: 7-zip, armoury-crate

Vendors: kaspersky, asus

EU sanctions pro-Russia hackers, two dozen staff at Kremlin disinformation contractor — Should Read

The EU sanctioned Russia’s Social Design Agency, 24 staff members, six pro-Kremlin media figures, and hacktivist group NoName057(16) for disinformation, election interference, and disruptive DDoS activity targeting European infrastructure and officials.

  • The European Union added 31 names to its sanctions regime targeting Russian destabilization activities, including the Social Design Agency, 24 of its staff members, and six pro-Kremlin commentators.
  • The Social Design Agency is accused of running the Doppelgänger disinformation campaign, which the EU says cloned news websites, created Wikipedia-style platforms, and staged physical provocations around the 2024 European parliamentary elections.
  • The new sanctions place the Social Design Agency under a legal regime aimed at operations against the EU, which could enable restrictions on transactions involving physical infrastructure such as servers and network equipment.
  • The EU said major Social Design Agency foreign-interference operations require approval from Sergey Kiriyenko, with officials including Sofia Zakharova overseeing daily work.
  • The European Council also sanctioned the pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16) over denial-of-service attacks targeting critical infrastructure and election candidates.

Lithuanian customs agency restores services after cyberattack, possible data breach — Should Read

Lithuanian Customs has partially restored services after a targeted cyberattack on its BAP portal, which may have exposed personal data belonging to several hundred users and businesses. The incident also disrupted access to EU customs systems, while investigators assess whether attackers reached deeper government infrastructure.

  • Lithuanian Customs partially restored online services after a cyberattack detected on November 10 forced it to shut down its BAP user-management portal.
  • The agency confirmed unauthorized access to BAP and said users who logged in on November 9 or 10 may have been affected by a potential personal-data breach.
  • Several hundred individuals and businesses, mostly based in Lithuania, may have been affected, although the agency said this does not confirm that their information was accessed, copied, or stolen.
  • The outage disrupted access to several European Commission customs platforms, including the Import Control System 2, while services used by customs intermediaries continued operating normally.
  • Lithuanian Customs notified national cybersecurity and data-protection authorities as well as relevant European Union institutions, and investigators have not identified the attackers or the vulnerability used.

Technologies: iam

Products: bap, import-control-system-2

Vendors: lithuanian-customs, european-commission

Australian retail giant Coles investigates cybersecurity incident — Should Read

Australian retailer Coles is investigating a cybersecurity incident and says it has found no evidence so far that customer, employee, or supplier data was stolen. Stores, online shopping, Flybuys, and subscriptions remain operational, though some Liquorland click-and-collect customers are affected.

  • Coles Group is investigating a cybersecurity incident and is working with the Australian Cyber Security Centre and external security experts to contain and secure its IT environment.
  • Coles says its investigation has not found evidence that customer, employee, or supplier data was compromised or removed from its systems.
  • Coles stores, online outlets, Flybuys accounts, Coles Plus, Coles Plus Delivery, and QuiteLike subscriptions have not been affected and customers can shop as normal.
  • Coles is aware of Liquorland click-and-collect issues affecting a small number of customers.
  • The company advised people to remain alert to suspicious requests for personal information and to use strong, unique passwords that are not reused across services.

Microsoft: Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support in 60 days — May Read

Windows Server 2016 will reach end of extended support on January 13, 2027, after which it will no longer receive regular security updates unless organizations enroll in Microsoft’s Extended Security Updates program. Microsoft recommends upgrading to Windows Server 2025.

  • All editions of Windows Server 2016 will reach the end of extended support on January 13, 2027, and the January 2027 security update will be the final update provided under that support period.
  • After January 13, 2027, monthly security updates for Windows Server 2016 will continue only for devices enrolled in Microsoft’s Extended Security Updates program.
  • Microsoft will also end support for Windows Server 2016 Essentials features, including Remote Web Access and related Essentials-specific functionality, on the same date.
  • Microsoft advises administrators to upgrade to Windows Server 2025, which is the latest Windows Server Long-Term Servicing Channel release.
  • Windows Server 2025 will receive mainstream support until November 2029 and extended support until November 14, 2034.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-server-2016, windows-server-2025, windows-11-24h2, windows-11-26h2, windows-10-enterprise-ltsc-2021, windows-11-enterprise-ltsc-2024

Vendors: microsoft

British government ‘complacent’ on cyber threats from hostile states, peers warn — May Read

A House of Lords committee warned that the UK is dangerously underprepared for cyber and other hostile-state threats from Russia, China and Iran, calling the government complacent. It said the delayed Cyber Security and Resilience Bill is too limited and urged broader regulation, stronger enforcement and greater public transparency.

  • The House of Lords National Resilience Committee said the United Kingdom is underprepared for potentially catastrophic risks, including cyberattacks from Russia, China and Iran.
  • The committee said the proposed Cyber Security and Resilience Bill would establish useful baseline requirements but has a limited scope and does not provide the necessary security standards to protect the country.
  • The report urged ministers to broaden cyber security regulation and ensure regulators have sufficient resources and capacity to enforce requirements.
  • The committee said the government appears complacent and should more directly inform the public about ongoing hostile activity, including cyberattacks and threats to undersea cables and pipelines.
  • Government Cyber Unit deputy director Michael Brunton-Spall told the committee that the government and public sector face critically high cyber and digital resilience risks and extremely low levels of resilience.

Health intel-sharing group warns industry in wake of cyberattack on French blood bank — May Read

Health-ISAC warned that cyberattacks on refrigeration controllers, including an incident affecting a major French blood bank, can directly threaten patient safety by endangering stored blood, plasma, and critical therapies.

  • Health-ISAC issued a security bulletin warning members about a recent wave of cyberattacks targeting refrigeration controllers.
  • The warning cited an incident that affected a major French blood bank.
  • Health-ISAC Chief Security Officer Errol Weiss said that manipulating cold-chain storage and refrigeration units can endanger donor blood, plasma, and critical therapies.
  • Weiss characterized cybersecurity in healthcare as fundamentally a patient-safety issue because attacks on operational technology can threaten physical resources needed to sustain human life.

Technologies: ics-scada

Google warns that fully-automated AI attacks are coming soon — Optional

Google says threat actors are increasingly using AI-powered multi-agent frameworks to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation, sharply reducing defenders’ time to patch. It expects low-touch attacks within three months and sophisticated fully autonomous campaigns within six months.

  • Google Threat Intelligence Group reported that threat actors are using AI-powered multi-agent frameworks to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation, including without a human in the loop.
  • Google estimates that low-complexity attacks requiring little to no human interaction could emerge within three months, while sophisticated fully autonomous attacks may appear within six months.
  • GTIG identified an exposed staging server for a multi-agent framework called exploit_agent that was used to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation against French media, entertainment, and education websites.
  • The FBI warned that multiple threat actors have weaponized the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework since August to target financial, government, technology, defense, healthcare, and other sectors.
  • Google also observed UNC6836, a cluster suspected of links to Midnight Neptune, using modified Claude Code to download the SOMBERMEME backdoor after compromising cryptocurrency firms in North America and Europe.

Products: cairn, claude-code, artex, cyberstrikeai, hexstrike-ai, exploit-agent

Vendors: google, anthropic

Tenable One Adversary View brings Claude Mythos’ adversarial reasoning to your environment — Optional

Tenable has made Adversary View generally available in Tenable One for Hexa AI users, using Claude Mythos to analyze existing scan data for attacker-style vulnerability chains and remediation choke points. It prioritizes patches and configuration changes by the number of attack paths they disrupt.

  • Tenable One Adversary View is generally available to Tenable One customers with Tenable Hexa AI.
  • Adversary View uses Claude Mythos to analyze existing vulnerability scan data and identify chains of weaknesses and routes an attacker could use through connected assets.
  • The feature ranks remediation actions by how many identified routes they close, rather than relying on severity ratings alone.
  • Users can scope an analysis to all assets or to tags, IP ranges, operating systems, or business units, and review scan evidence supporting each step of a route.
  • Adversary View can generate Jira tickets, remediation dashboards, and downloadable PDF reports for identified findings.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: tenable-one, tenable-hexa-ai, claude-mythos, windows-server-2016, windows-server-2022, jira

Vendors: tenable, anthropic, microsoft, atlassian

16th November – Threat Intelligence Report — Optional

Check Point’s 16 November threat report highlights major breaches at TSMC, Maersk, Osaka and ConnectWise alongside growing AI-assisted intrusion activity. It also warns of actively exploited flaws in Check Point gateways, Microsoft Outlook and Google Chrome, urging organizations to patch exposed systems promptly.

  • TSMC confirmed a breach at an unnamed cloud provider that exposed current and former employee information, while stating that its own systems and customer data were unaffected.
  • Maersk confirmed unauthorized access and data theft from a legacy system acquired through an acquisition, and the WhiteArmor group claimed to have stolen about 100 GB of information.
  • Researchers reported AI-assisted intrusions involving DeepSeek and Zhipu GLM agents that targeted at least 19 organizations and compromised 10 of them.
  • Check Point Research traced attacks exploiting PHP2Shell through unpatched Mobile Access portals on Check Point Security Gateways, followed by privilege escalation using CVE-2026-123039.
  • Microsoft, Google, and Apache released fixes for serious vulnerabilities, including actively exploited flaws affecting Outlook and Google Chrome.

Technologies: firewall, remote-access, browser, web-server, network-monitoring, hypervisor

Products: check-point-security-gateway, mobile-access, screenconnect, outlook, google-chrome, apache-http-server, solarwinds-orion, vmware-esxi, deepseek, zhipu-glm

Vendors: check-point, connectwise, microsoft, google, apache-software-foundation, solarwinds, vmware, deepseek, zhipu-ai

item.title: SANSAR Mining Rootkit, NoisyTCP Linux Flaw, and AI Agent API-Key Campaign
item.content:encoded:
Window: 16 Nov 07:00 → 16 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

SANSAR Linux Cryptomining Malware Uses Modified NVIDIA Library to Hide GPU Activity — Should Read

Elastic Security Labs reports that the REF3364 cryptomining operation uses the Rust-based SANSAR toolkit, a Linux kernel rootkit, and a modified NVIDIA NVML library to mine cryptocurrency while hiding processes, files, network activity, and GPU utilization. The attackers reportedly gain access through exposed Ray job agents and maintain control via TOR-based C2 and an Ethereum smart-contract-assisted backdoor.

  • Elastic Security Labs attributed a Linux-focused cryptocurrency-mining operation to a financially motivated cluster tracked as REF3364, which uses a Rust-based toolkit named SANSAR.
  • The documented attack chain began with an exposed Ray job agent, which attackers used to run commands, inventory GPUs, establish a reverse shell, and add an SSH key for persistent access.
  • After obtaining root access, the attackers installed the acpi_thermal_mgr kernel module through DKMS and an initramfs loader so the rootkit could reload when the host booted.
  • A modified NVIDIA Management Library wrapper causes tools such as nvidia-smi to report zero GPU utilization and replaces temperature and power readings with randomized values.
  • SANSAR uses a TOR onion service for command-and-control, while the netns backdoor obtains a controller address from an Ethereum smart contract and connects to it on TCP port 8080.

Technologies: orchestration, operating-system

Products: ray, nvidia-management-library, nvidia-smi, linux, xmrig, srbminer-multi, arti

Vendors: nvidia, anscale, tor-project, elastic

Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys — Should Read

Amazon observed attackers using ARTEX AI agents to rapidly scan exposed AI application platforms such as LiteLLM, Dify, and RAGFlow for default credentials, unpatched flaws, and leaked API keys. The campaign highlights that internet-facing AI gateways and static CI/CD tokens can expose high-value provider credentials unless organizations patch systems, rotate secrets, and enforce strong access controls.

  • Amazon Threat Intelligence captured records from AI agents that targeted internet-exposed AI applications, including LiteLLM, One API, and Dify, to obtain stored AI-provider keys.
  • Amazon assessed with moderate confidence that the agents used ARTEX, an open-source AI penetration-testing tool, although it could not verify the outcomes the agents reported from systems outside its decoy network.
  • The captured playbook included default administrator credentials, unfinished installations, unauthenticated management endpoints, an isCliRequest-header authentication bypass in One API family systems, and server-side request forgery paths to cloud metadata services.
  • Cloudflare investigated an ARTEX-related incident involving a compromised account-level API token used for CI/CD, followed by the creation of Worker scripts and roughly 400 database-dump requests within an hour.
  • Amazon recommended that organizations change default credentials, remove and rotate exposed secrets, patch affected software, and monitor AI services for unexpected spending or unusual usage.

Technologies: api-gateway, cloud-platform, ci-cd, secrets-manager

Products: aws, madpot, cloudflare-workers, litellm, dify, one-api, new-api, veloera, sub2api, fastgpt, langflow, ragflow, open-webui, lobechat, ollama, artex

Vendors: amazon, cloudflare, microsoft, infiniflow, litellm, dify, one-api, langflow, open-webui, ollama

New NoisyTCP vulnerability lets attackers crash Linux servers — Should Read

Researchers disclosed NoisyTCP (CVE-2026-99288), an 11-year-old Linux kernel flaw that lets unauthenticated remote attackers crash affected Linux servers by triggering a TCP race condition. A mainline kernel fix is available; organizations should patch promptly or mitigate by disabling SYN cookies or using a single RX queue if patching is not immediately possible.

  • NoisyTCP, tracked as CVE-2026-99288, is an 11-year-old Linux kernel flaw that can allow unauthenticated remote attackers to crash affected systems using crafted TCP packets.
  • The flaw is caused by a race condition involving SYN cookie handling and socket hashing that can lead to a NULL pointer dereference and a kernel panic.
  • Linux systems that receive TCP packets directly and run Nginx, Apache, or an SSH server may be affected, especially systems with two or more receive queues or traffic distributed across multiple CPUs.
  • The reported impact is denial of service: the vulnerability can crash the host but does not allow attackers to alter data or execute arbitrary code.
  • A fix has been merged into the mainline Linux kernel, and temporary mitigations include disabling SYN cookies or using a single receive queue when immediate patching is not possible.

Technologies: operating-system, web-server, remote-access

Products: linux-kernel, nginx, apache-http-server, openssh

Vendors: linux-kernel, red-hat, debian, nginx, apache-software-foundation, openssh

A USB worm’s second life: Retadup spreading CoffeeLoader — Should Read

A revived Retadup USB worm infrastructure is distributing a new CoffeeLoader variant that uses an OpenGL-based Armoury packer, persistence via Run registry keys, process injection, and signed HTTPS payload downloads. The campaign has affected roughly 15,000 systems, primarily in Peru, Angola, Russia, and Bolivia.

  • Kaspersky detected a new CoffeeLoader variant in August 2026 that uses a patched 7-Zip library and a new Armoury packer variant to decrypt malicious code with the GPU through OpenGL.
  • The CoffeeLoader downloader establishes persistence by copying itself into ProgramData or LocalAppData, creating a Windows Run registry entry, and launching or injecting into processes such as dllhost.exe, WerFault.exe, svchost.exe, OpenWith.exe, or AtBroker.exe.
  • The downloader retrieves CoffeeLoader's main component over HTTPS from a hardcoded command-and-control server, verifies the downloaded data using an embedded public key and an MD5 checksum, and then runs the decrypted code.
  • CoffeeLoader is being distributed through revived Retadup command-and-control domains that issue commands to older Retadup infections, including infections spread through USB drives and shortcut files.
  • Kaspersky blocked Retadup infection attempts on around 15,000 systems during the first three quarters of 2026, with most detections in Peru, Angola, Russia, and Bolivia.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows, 7-zip, nsis

Vendors: kaspersky, microsoft

Microsoft pushes Windows emergency updates to fix activation failures — Should Read

Microsoft released emergency out-of-band updates for Windows 10, Windows 11 23H2, and Windows Server to fix activation and licensing failures introduced by November security updates, primarily affecting organizations that automate licensing with Slmgr.vbs.

  • Microsoft released emergency out-of-band Windows updates to address activation and licensing failures caused by the November security updates.
  • The issue affects organizations that use the Slmgr.vbs command-line tool to automate Windows activation and licensing processes.
  • Devices that are already activated are expected to remain activated, and customers with the appropriate KMS client key and configuration who do not run affected Slmgr.vbs commands are not expected to be affected.
  • The emergency updates cover Windows Server 2019, 2022, and 2025, Windows 10 21H2 and 22H2 variants, and Windows 11 version 23H2.
  • Most of the out-of-band updates are available only through the Microsoft Update Catalog, while the Windows 11 23H2 update is also available as an optional Windows Update.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-10, windows-11, windows-server-2019, windows-server-2022, windows-server-2025, slmgr-vbs, key-management-service

Vendors: microsoft

Health-ISAC Daily Cyber Headlines – November 16, 2026 — Optional

Health-ISAC’s November 16, 2026 roundup highlights active exploitation of a Check Point zero-day alongside an Apify breach, ARTEX-enabled attacks, Windows and Linux flaws, proposed HIPAA Privacy Rule changes, and growing cyber incidents in Singapore’s health sector.

  • The roundup includes an Apify breach and ARTEX-enabled attacks.
  • The article addresses Windows and Linux vulnerabilities.

  • The roundup reports rising cyber incidents affecting Singapore’s health sector.

item.title: FBI Flags ARTEX AI Attacks; TSMC Employee Data Exposed via Cloud Provider
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Nov 15:00 → 15 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks — Must Read

The FBI warns that threat actors are using the ARTEX AI-driven penetration-testing framework to automate global intrusions at unprecedented speed, including the ConnectWise supply-chain compromise affecting Microsoft 365 tenants. Organizations should monitor for ARTEX-related indicators and unusual automated, cloud, identity, and data-transfer activity.

  • The FBI warned that multiple threat actors have used the AI-powered ARTEX penetration-testing framework since at least August 2026 to target organizations in financial, government, technology, defense, healthcare, and other sectors.
  • ARTEX uses external AI models and specialized agents to automate tasks such as finding targets, identifying weaknesses, gaining access, escalating privileges, and stealing data.
  • The FBI said some ARTEX-enabled intrusions progressed from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours, while allowing attackers to conduct operations against multiple targets simultaneously.
  • ARTEX was linked to the October ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain attack, in which compromised application identities were used to access Microsoft 365 customer environments.
  • The FBI advisory provides ARTEX-related indicators and recommends that organizations monitor for unusual automated requests, suspicious cloud activity, unexpected credential or privilege changes, and large data transfers.

Technologies: cloud-platform, backup, iam

Products: artex, connectwise-cloud-backup, microsoft-365, claude-code

Vendors: connectwise, microsoft, anthropic, crowdstrike

TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider — Should Read

TSMC confirmed that personal data belonging to current and former employees was exposed through a cloud service provider, while stating there is no evidence its own systems or customer operations were compromised. A threat actor calling itself SmithBianl is auctioning an alleged 6.9GB dataset containing roughly 46,000 employee records.

  • TSMC confirmed that unauthorized online material included personal data belonging to some current and former employees.
  • TSMC said the leaked data matched information stored in the system services of a cloud service provider and that it found no evidence its own systems were compromised.
  • A threat actor using the alias SmithBianl claimed to have a 6.9GB dataset containing 46,000 TSMC employee records and offered it for auction starting at 3 BTC.
  • The alleged dataset includes national ID numbers, addresses, contact information, and banking details.
  • TSMC is notifying affected staff, providing support, and working with a third-party cybersecurity firm.

Technologies: cloud-platform

item.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook Android Gallery Access
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Nov 11:00 → 15 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent — Should Read

Italy’s data protection authority fined Meta €805 million for Facebook’s Android gallery-suggestion feature, finding it accessed users’ photo libraries by default without specific, informed consent. Meta must disable the feature by default and obtain separate consent within 60 days, while it plans to appeal.

  • Italy’s data protection authority fined Meta €805 million over Facebook for Android’s gallery-suggestion feature.
  • The authority found that the feature was enabled by default and accessed users’ photos, videos, and related metadata without separate, explicit consent.
  • Meta has 60 days to disable the feature by default, including for users who previously granted gallery access, and to obtain specific consent through a separate request.
  • The investigation concerned roughly 20 million Android users in Italy and found that the breach remains ongoing for some users.
  • Meta said it will appeal the decision and maintains that users grant device permission and can change it at any time.

Technologies: mobile-os

Products: facebook, android

Vendors: meta, google

item.title: Cursor Details Fireworks AI Key Exposure and Trojanized Claude Code Extension
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Nov 07:00 → 15 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident — Should Read

Cursor says a stolen Fireworks AI access key exposed limited customer and internal data, including some credentials, which an attacker later used to distribute a trojanized Claude Code extension through Cursor Marketplace. Up to 5,000 users may have received the malicious build during an 11-hour window on October 29, 2026.

  • Cursor said an attacker used an access key issued to Fireworks AI, which Fireworks exposed, to copy data from a read-only storage bucket shared with the provider.
  • The storage bucket contained limited coding-agent session traces from users who had not enabled Privacy Mode, and fewer than 0.01% of customers had API credentials exposed in those traces.
  • The attacker used credentials from the exposed data to access select Cursor SaaS tools, obtaining archived non-production source-code repositories, limited support data, usage metrics, coding conversation summaries, and some credentials submitted to support.
  • On October 29, 2026, the attacker used a stolen internal credential to place trojanized Claude Code extension versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 in Cursor Marketplace, where they were available for about 11 hours.
  • Cursor said up to 5,000 users may have received the malicious extension build and that it found no additional malicious activity after November 1, 2026.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: cursor-marketplace, claude-code

Vendors: cursor, fireworks-ai, anthropic

item.title: LiteLLM, OVHcloud, Cursor and AI Plugin Supply-Chain Security Incidents
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Nov 00:00 → 16 Nov 00:00 UTC (1 day)

litellm 1.107.0 Compromised on PyPI and Docker: Credential Stealer and Hourly Remote Code Loader — Must Read

LiteLLM 1.107.0 PyPI wheels and official Docker images were compromised with a Python startup-hook credential stealer and hourly remote-code loader, exposing cloud, browser, SSH, AI-tool, CI, and proxy database secrets. Anyone who installed or ran the affected artifacts on October 21, 2026 should treat the host as fully compromised, rebuild it, and rotate all reachable credentials.

  • All seven PyPI wheels for LiteLLM 1.107.0 and the associated official Docker images contained cook.pth, cook.py, and sitecustomize.py, which ran automatically when Python started without requiring an import of LiteLLM.
  • The embedded privcollect payload collected browser data, SSH and GPG keys, cloud credentials, process environment variables, AI coding-tool credentials, and LiteLLM proxy database credentials, then sent an encrypted bundle to www.litellm.dev.
  • A second payload created a detached background process on Linux and macOS that checked an attacker-controlled GitHub location every hour and could download and execute Python code.
  • BerriAI reported that an unrecalled master key exposed in a public repository enabled theft of a GitHub organization owner token, which was then used to steal CI secrets and alter the release workflow to build from a lookalike repository.
  • Organizations that installed LiteLLM 1.107.0 from a wheel or ran affected Docker images are advised to treat the host as compromised, rebuild affected environments, and rotate every credential the host could access.

Technologies: api-gateway, package-registry, ci-cd, source-control, container-platform, cloud-platform

Products: litellm, pypi, github-actions, github-container-registry, docker-hub, harden-runner

Vendors: berriai, github, docker, amazon-web-services, stepsecurity

FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks — Must Read

The FBI warns that threat actors are using the ARTEX AI-driven penetration-testing framework to automate global intrusions at unprecedented speed, including the ConnectWise supply-chain compromise affecting Microsoft 365 tenants. Organizations should monitor for ARTEX-related indicators and unusual automated, cloud, identity, and data-transfer activity.

  • The FBI warned that multiple threat actors have used the AI-powered ARTEX penetration-testing framework since at least August 2026 to target organizations in financial, government, technology, defense, healthcare, and other sectors.
  • ARTEX uses external AI models and specialized agents to automate tasks such as finding targets, identifying weaknesses, gaining access, escalating privileges, and stealing data.
  • The FBI said some ARTEX-enabled intrusions progressed from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours, while allowing attackers to conduct operations against multiple targets simultaneously.
  • ARTEX was linked to the October ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain attack, in which compromised application identities were used to access Microsoft 365 customer environments.
  • The FBI advisory provides ARTEX-related indicators and recommends that organizations monitor for unusual automated requests, suspicious cloud activity, unexpected credential or privilege changes, and large data transfers.

Technologies: cloud-platform, backup, iam

Products: artex, connectwise-cloud-backup, microsoft-365, claude-code

Vendors: connectwise, microsoft, anthropic, crowdstrike

OVHcloud CLI Compromised via GitHub Release Swap: Detonating the Real GlassWorm Loader and What We Found — Should Read

Attackers used a compromised OVHcloud contributor account to replace binaries for five ovhcloud-cli GitHub releases for 94 minutes, deploying the GlassWorm credential stealer to roughly 250 downloads. Anyone who ran a directly downloaded or script-installed affected binary should treat the host as compromised and rotate all accessible secrets from a separate machine.

  • On October 19, 2026, an attacker using the GitHub account HassenBF replaced binaries on OVHcloud CLI releases v0.11.0 through v0.15.0 for 94 minutes without moving release tags or modifying the source repository.
  • The swapped binaries contained a credential stealer that collected AI-agent credential stores, cloud and container credentials, SSH keys, and configuration files, staged them in /tmp/envchecker-* directories, and sent an archive to 45.32.148.174/upload.
  • The affected release assets were locally built from commit 5ead8ef with a plain stripped Go build rather than the official release pipeline, causing ovhcloud version to report an undefined version and the attacker’s build commit.
  • OVHcloud removed the swapped assets, published a clean immutable and attested v0.16.0 release, and reported approximately 250 downloads.
  • Homebrew installations were not exposed because its cask pinned SHA-256 hashes and would reject swapped files, while arm64 Linux users relying only on install.sh were not exposed because that script’s arm64 asset request always returned a 404 error.

Technologies: source-control, package-registry

Products: ovhcloud-cli, github-releases, homebrew-cask, visual-studio-code, color-picker-universal

Vendors: ovhcloud, github, homebrew, microsoft, solana

eMudhra / emSign CA Compromise: What Python, pip, and CI/CD Users Need to Update — Should Read

Update Python package tooling and certificate bundles immediately: compromised eMudhra/emSign intermediate CA keys could enable HTTPS impersonation of package indexes for clients that still trust affected chains. Upgrade certifi to 2026.10.19+, pip to 26.2.2+, and update uv, conda, Pixi, CI images, and any custom trust stores.

  • Google reported that eight eMudhra/emSign intermediate certificate authority keys were generated with insufficient randomness, potentially allowing recovered keys to issue certificates impersonating websites.
  • Python users should update certifi to 2026.10.19 or later and pip to 26.2.2 or later, while also updating affected uv, sigstore, conda, and Pixi installations.
  • Updating a project's standalone certifi package does not update pip's separately bundled certificate store, so pip itself must be updated.
  • Testing described in the article found that certifi 2026.10.19 and pip 26.2.2 rejected all fourteen published affected certificate chains, while certifi 2026.07.22 accepted seven of them.
  • Organizations should rebuild containers and CI images, review custom certificate settings, and verify rejection using the actual client and trust configuration used by their workloads.

Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident — Should Read

Cursor says a stolen Fireworks AI access key exposed limited customer and internal data, including some credentials, which an attacker later used to distribute a trojanized Claude Code extension through Cursor Marketplace. Up to 5,000 users may have received the malicious build during an 11-hour window on October 29, 2026.

  • Cursor said an attacker used an access key issued to Fireworks AI, which Fireworks exposed, to copy data from a read-only storage bucket shared with the provider.
  • The storage bucket contained limited coding-agent session traces from users who had not enabled Privacy Mode, and fewer than 0.01% of customers had API credentials exposed in those traces.
  • The attacker used credentials from the exposed data to access select Cursor SaaS tools, obtaining archived non-production source-code repositories, limited support data, usage metrics, coding conversation summaries, and some credentials submitted to support.
  • On October 29, 2026, the attacker used a stolen internal credential to place trojanized Claude Code extension versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 in Cursor Marketplace, where they were available for about 11 hours.
  • Cursor said up to 5,000 users may have received the malicious extension build and that it found no additional malicious activity after November 1, 2026.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: cursor-marketplace, claude-code

Vendors: cursor, fireworks-ai, anthropic

TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider — Should Read

TSMC confirmed that personal data belonging to current and former employees was exposed through a cloud service provider, while stating there is no evidence its own systems or customer operations were compromised. A threat actor calling itself SmithBianl is auctioning an alleged 6.9GB dataset containing roughly 46,000 employee records.

  • TSMC confirmed that unauthorized online material included personal data belonging to some current and former employees.
  • TSMC said the leaked data matched information stored in the system services of a cloud service provider and that it found no evidence its own systems were compromised.
  • A threat actor using the alias SmithBianl claimed to have a 6.9GB dataset containing 46,000 TSMC employee records and offered it for auction starting at 3 BTC.
  • The alleged dataset includes national ID numbers, addresses, contact information, and banking details.
  • TSMC is notifying affected staff, providing support, and working with a third-party cybersecurity firm.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent — Should Read

Italy’s data protection authority fined Meta €805 million for Facebook’s Android gallery-suggestion feature, finding it accessed users’ photo libraries by default without specific, informed consent. Meta must disable the feature by default and obtain separate consent within 60 days, while it plans to appeal.

  • Italy’s data protection authority fined Meta €805 million over Facebook for Android’s gallery-suggestion feature.
  • The authority found that the feature was enabled by default and accessed users’ photos, videos, and related metadata without separate, explicit consent.
  • Meta has 60 days to disable the feature by default, including for users who previously granted gallery access, and to obtain specific consent through a separate request.
  • The investigation concerned roughly 20 million Android users in Italy and found that the breach remains ongoing for some users.
  • Meta said it will appeal the decision and maintains that users grant device permission and can change it at any time.

Technologies: mobile-os

Products: facebook, android

Vendors: meta, google

The Bounce Was Real. The Message Inside It Was the Phish. — May Read

A legitimate university bounce notice passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and compauth, but those results authenticated only the bounce—not the spoofed voicemail phishing email quoted inside it. Analysts must inspect authentication headers within bounced content, where the original showed SPF and DMARC failures with no DKIM signature.

  • A Canadian electrical engineer received an authentic university delivery-failure notice that passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and compauth checks.
  • The authentication passes applied to the university-generated bounce notice, not to the spoofed message reproduced within its body.
  • The quoted original message showed SPF failure, DMARC failure, no DKIM signature, and a client-supplied loopback HELO value of [127.0.0.1].
  • The quoted lure used a secure-document subject and a voicemail-themed body with a Call Back button, but it reached the recipient as plain text with no rendered clickable link.
  • The record does not establish how the bounce was routed to the engineer's mailbox or whether the engineer was deliberately targeted.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: exchange-online, onedrive, adaptive-ai

Vendors: microsoft, ironscales

StepSecurity Now Inventories AI Agent Plugins in Your GitHub Repositories and on Developer Machines — Optional

StepSecurity has launched inventories for Claude Code and Codex plugins installed on developer machines and published or enabled in GitHub repositories, helping organizations trace plugin sources, components, versions, and usage. The feature addresses AI agent plugins as a supply-chain risk because they can run hooks and code with developer privileges and propagate through repositories and marketplaces.

  • StepSecurity introduced Agent Plugins inventories in Dev Machine Guard for Claude Code and Codex plugins installed on developer machines, and under GitHub for plugins that organization repositories publish or enable.
  • The Dev Machine Guard inventory shows a plugin’s declared publisher, marketplace and file source, observed versions, enabled or disabled status, supplied components, and devices where it is installed.
  • AI agent plugins can execute code with the developer’s user privileges, including hooks and locally started tool connections, and may access machines holding SSH keys, cloud credentials, and publishing tokens.
  • The GitHub inventory identifies plugins from their manifests, including plugins in repository subfolders, and shows the publishing repository, path, version, supplied components, and repositories that enable each plugin.
  • StepSecurity distinguishes self-declared manifest metadata from observed plugin sources, helping users investigate cases where a plugin’s stated author or repository differs from the repository that publishes it.

Technologies: source-control, package-registry

Products: dev-machine-guard, claude-code, codex, github, jetbrains-marketplace

Vendors: stepsecurity, anthropic, openai, github, jetbrains, microsoft

GitHub Actions Native Egress Firewall vs. Harden-Runner: Five Differences That Matter — Optional

StepSecurity argues that Harden-Runner provides broader CI/CD runner protection than GitHub’s native egress firewall, adding cross-platform coverage, behavioral and file-write monitoring, threat-intelligence blocking, and centralized policy enforcement. The article positions it as a runtime security solution for both GitHub-hosted and self-hosted runners.

  • GitHub’s native egress firewall preview supports GitHub-hosted Linux runners, while StepSecurity’s Harden-Runner supports Linux, Windows, and macOS on GitHub-hosted and self-hosted runners.
  • Harden-Runner builds network baselines from prior workflow runs and flags new destinations, correlating network, process, and file events with the workflow step involved.
  • StepSecurity states that Harden-Runner blocks connections to endpoints on its Global Block List even in audit mode and can terminate processes or stop jobs through Lockdown Mode when suspicious behavior is detected.
  • Harden-Runner monitors file writes during jobs and flags changes to checked-out source files, which StepSecurity says can help detect build tampering that network-only controls cannot observe.
  • The article states that organizations can use Harden-Runner’s centralized dashboard, API, and MCP server to identify jobs that directly contact public package registries and apply deny policies to prevent bypassing approved registries.

Technologies: ci-cd, firewall, package-registry, container-platform, object-storage, source-control, siem

item.title: Cursor Claude Code Extension Breach and BlueNoroff FaceStealer Disruption
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Nov 15:00 → 14 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension — Should Read

Cursor confirmed that attackers used credentials exposed through Fireworks AI and leaked coding-agent traces to access internal systems and publish trojanized Claude Code extensions that attempted to install persistent SSH backdoors. Up to 5,000 developers may have downloaded the malicious builds during their roughly 11-hour availability window.

  • Cursor said attackers obtained an access key stored on Fireworks AI and used it to copy data from a read-only storage bucket shared with the provider.
  • Historical AI coding-agent traces in the bucket included unredacted API credentials in some cases, which attackers used to access additional Cursor systems and data from several SaaS tools.
  • On October 29, attackers used a stolen credential to publish malicious versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 of Anthropic's Claude Code extension through Cursor's marketplace cache.
  • The malicious extensions were available for about 11 hours and attempted to install persistent SSH backdoors, with Cursor estimating that up to 5,000 users may have received them.
  • Cursor said it revoked and rotated exposed credentials, moved inference traffic away from Fireworks, rebuilt its extension marketplace, and redeployed production infrastructure.

Technologies: package-registry, object-storage, cloud-platform

Products: cursor, claude-code, visual-studio-code, open-vsx

Vendors: cursor, fireworks-ai, anthropic, microsoft

US disrupts North Korean campaign behind $400 million crypto theft — Should Read

U.S. authorities disrupted FaceStealer, a BlueNoroff-linked North Korean social-engineering campaign that used deepfake video meetings and fake technical fixes to steal more than $400 million in cryptocurrency and compromise crypto professionals and open-source developers.

  • The U.S. government disrupted the cloud-based infrastructure behind FaceStealer, an 18-month North Korean social-engineering campaign linked by researchers to the BlueNoroff group that stole more than $400 million in cryptocurrency.
  • FaceStealer operators hijacked Telegram, LinkedIn, Slack, and Discord accounts to invite targets to fake video meetings, where they used recorded footage of people known to the target and then presented a fake technical error.
  • Victims who followed links for supposed updates or installers were infected with software that could steal cryptocurrency data, meeting-platform credentials, contact lists, social-media and communication-app access, and webcam recordings.
  • Researchers identified 677 targets in 58 countries, primarily company founders and senior executives, while the FBI also confirmed attempts against developers in the npm and Rust crate ecosystems.
  • The U.S. Justice Department said that the government and private-sector companies froze more than $2.7 billion connected to the $6.4 billion Binance crypto heist, with court authorization obtained to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion.

item.title: CISA Flags Actively Exploited UnrealIRCd CVE-2026-114713 Command Injection
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Nov 11:00 → 14 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection — Must Read

CISA added CVE-2026-114713, a critical UnrealIRCd flaw actively exploited to inject server-to-server commands with server-level privileges, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Organizations should urgently upgrade to UnrealIRCd 6.2.7.1 or apply the available workaround.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-114713, an actively exploited high-severity UnrealIRCd flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
  • The flaw affects UnrealIRCd versions 6.0.0 through versions before 6.2.7.1 and can allow users to inject server-to-server commands with server-level privileges on networks with at least two linked servers.
  • UnrealIRCd released version 6.2.7.1 to address CVE-2026-114713 and other security issues.
  • The UnrealIRCd maintainer said exploitation began a day after the November 7, 2026 hotfix release and described it as the project’s most critical issue in 15 years.
  • Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must apply fixes by November 16, 2026 under Binding Operational Directive 26-04.

Products: unrealircd

Vendors: unrealircd-project, cisa

Fake Purview Card: Three Footer Links, One Tutorial Page — May Read

A phishing email convincingly impersonated Microsoft Purview Message Encryption, but its Read the message button and legal footer links all led to the same newly created tutorial-hosted page. The key lesson is to hover footer links as well as action buttons: a genuine Purview message routes them to distinct Microsoft destinations.

  • A counterfeit Microsoft Purview Message Encryption email reached four employees at a manufacturer, including the Italian general manager.
  • The email's Read the message button, Privacy Statement link, and Learn More link all led to the same page on a public tutorial-builder site, unlike a genuine Purview wrapper.
  • The message passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and ARC checks because it was sent from the sender organization's authenticated Microsoft 365 tenant.
  • The linked tutorial page displayed an Italian fake protected-file notice and a document-viewing button, and it was created about two days before capture.
  • A human analyst classified the email as malicious and quarantined all four affected mailboxes.

ESLint Ends Paid Contributor Program as AI Upends Open Source Collaboration — Optional

ESLint has ended its five-year paid contributor program after AI-generated pull requests and disputes over disclosure made it too burdensome to determine which work deserved compensation. The move reflects a broader open-source shift toward stricter contribution controls as maintainers struggle with AI-driven review volume and low-quality submissions.

  • ESLint ended its paid contributor pool after five years, citing the difficulty of handling AI-generated issues and pull requests and disputes over undisclosed AI use.
  • From 2022 through 2025, ESLint paid outside contributors $51,180 through the program, including $24,680 in 2025.
  • ESLint still permits AI-assisted contributions when their use is disclosed, the contributor reviews the work, and the contributor remains responsible for the submission.
  • Several open-source projects, including Godot, LLVM, tldraw, Node.js, and the Linux kernel, have introduced restrictions or additional requirements in response to the review burden created by AI-generated submissions.
  • A Linux Foundation study published in October found that 59% of surveyed maintainers reported growing generative-AI-related contributions, while respondents estimated that 25% of incoming pull requests were low-quality AI-generated submissions.

Technologies: source-control

item.title: FBI Warns of ARTEX AI Intrusion Automation as Framework Spreads Widely
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Nov 19:00 → 13 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms — Should Read

Cisco Talos reports that ARTEX, an AI-enabled penetration-testing framework, is being abused by criminal and China-linked actors to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, cloud abuse, and post-compromise activity at machine speed. Organizations should prioritize identity and secrets protection, monitoring for rapid anomalous activity, and preplanned containment measures.

  • Cisco Talos reports that ARTEX is an AI-enabled penetration-testing framework that can use planner and worker agents to automate reconnaissance, vulnerability testing, and follow-on actions with limited operator input.
  • Public reporting and Talos observations associate ARTEX activity with financially motivated cybercriminals and China-nexus actors, including VAPOR PANDA, Storm-0940, and Storm-3358.
  • Reported ARTEX campaigns have used password spraying, exposed or stolen credentials, and application or authorization flaws to target organizations in sectors including government, finance, telecommunications, defense, pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and technology.
  • Talos identified more than 2,500 ARTEX-associated C2 IP addresses and observed overlapping infrastructure with tools including VShell, AdaptixC2, Mimikatz, Cobalt Strike, GoPhish, and Fscan.
  • Talos recommends protecting credentials and exposed secrets, hardening public-facing systems and cloud resources, monitoring for rapid unusual activity, and preparing procedures for fast containment.

Technologies: orchestration, cloud-platform, secrets-manager, identity-provider, source-control, remote-access

Products: artex, pentagi, hephaestus, microsoft-365, azure-key-vault, amazon-cognito, amazon-s3, amazon-cloudwatch, connectwise

Vendors: cisco, microsoft, connectwise, amazon-web-services, github

City of Osaka warns of data breach impacting 1 million as Japan reels from dozens of cyber incidents — Should Read

A breach of Arara’s email distribution service exposed more than 1 million email addresses linked to Osaka’s administrative platform and potentially 77 million addresses across nearly 400 Japanese organizations. The incident is part of a wider surge in cyberattacks prompting Japan to fund stronger national cyber defenses and faster breach reporting.

  • Osaka said that hackers accessed Arara’s email distribution service, used by TKC Corporation for the city’s online administrative services platform, exposing more than 1 million email addresses.
  • The city said the leaked addresses belonged to people who received emails from its system between July 2026 and October 31, and warned residents not to open suspicious links or attachments in messages claiming to be from Osaka.
  • Arara said a November 2 cyberattack exposed 77 million email addresses from nearly 400 customers, including TKC and Sega, and was used to send millions of malicious emails impersonating credit card companies and financial institutions.
  • Japan’s prime minister announced emergency cybersecurity measures, including increased use of AI for defense, stronger information gathering, offensive cyber operations, victim support, and about $62 million in emergency funding.
  • Mihoko Matsubara of NTT said October accounted for 58% of Japan’s reported cyber incidents this year and that about 380 million pieces of personal data had been stolen so far this year.

Products: arara-email-distribution-service

Vendors: arara, tkc

Trezor confirms crypto-stealing implants in three wallets, releases fix — Should Read

Trezor confirmed that three Safe 5 wallets sold by Indonesian reseller CryptoBilis contained cellular-connected hardware implants that could steal recovery phrases and passphrases. Firmware 2.13.1 blocks the known implants, but affected buyers should move funds to a new wallet because previously captured recovery phrases remain exposed.

  • Trezor confirmed that three Safe 5 wallets sold by Indonesian reseller CryptoBilis contained malicious hardware implants designed to capture recovery phrases and passphrases.
  • The implants used an extra circuit board between the wallet’s main board and display to monitor screen activity, encrypt captured information, and send it through a mobile network to an attacker-controlled server.
  • Trezor released firmware version 2.13.1 on November 11, which it says prevents the identified implants from capturing information on updated devices.
  • The update cannot protect recovery phrases that may have been captured before installation, and Trezor advises CryptoBilis customers to move cryptocurrency to a newly created wallet with a new recovery phrase.
  • Trezor reduced its global reseller network by about 80% and is offering replacement devices to customers who purchased a Trezor wallet from CryptoBilis since March 2026.

Products: trezor-safe-5, trezor-firmware-2-13-1

Vendors: trezor, cryptobilis, ledger
